We need to use integration by parts. We'll work out the indefinite integral first, and then proceed to work out the definite integral.

In this case, we define

$$
\begin{aligned}u=4{x}^{2}+3\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=8x \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=\operatorname{sin}⁡x\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x=\int \operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x=-\operatorname{cos}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula for integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (4{x}^{2}+3)\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =(4{x}^{2}+3)(-\operatorname{cos}⁡x)-\int (-\operatorname{cos}⁡x)(8x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =-(4{x}^{2}+3)\operatorname{cos}⁡x+8\int x\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Again, we use integration by parts to evaluate $\int x\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\text{d}x.$ We take

$$
\begin{aligned}u=x & \,⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=1\,, \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=\operatorname{cos}⁡x & \,⟹\,v=\int \operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\text{d}x=\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,.\end{aligned}
$$

In this case, the formula for integration by parts gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\int x\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =x\operatorname{sin}⁡x-\int \operatorname{sin}⁡x\,dx \\  & =x\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\operatorname{cos}⁡x+D,\end{aligned}
$$

where $D$ is an integral constant. 

So, we get that the indefinite integral is

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (4{x}^{2}+3)\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x & =-(4{x}^{2}+3)\operatorname{cos}⁡x+8\int x\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =-(4{x}^{2}+3)\operatorname{cos}⁡x+8(x\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\operatorname{cos}⁡x+D) \\  & =-(4{x}^{2}+3)\operatorname{cos}⁡x+8x\operatorname{sin}⁡x+8\operatorname{cos}⁡x+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C=8D.$

Finally, we can work out the definite integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi }(4{x}^{2}+3)\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x & ={[-(4{x}^{2}+3)\operatorname{cos}⁡x+8x\operatorname{sin}⁡x+8\operatorname{cos}⁡x]}_{0}^{\pi } \\  & =(-(4{\pi }^{2}+3)\operatorname{cos}⁡\pi +8\pi \operatorname{sin}⁡\pi +8\operatorname{cos}⁡\pi )-(-3\operatorname{cos}⁡0+8(0)\operatorname{sin}⁡0+8\operatorname{cos}⁡0) \\  & =(4{\pi }^{2}+3-8)-(-3+8) \\  & =4{\pi }^{2}-5-5 \\  & =4{\pi }^{2}-10\end{aligned}
$$
